name: The Threefold Office (Prophet, Priest, and King)

objectives.text: Identify Jesus as our Prophet, Priest, and King
Describe from John 10 how Jesus, the Good Shepherd, leads, protects, and cares for His sheep
Recall Gospel examples of Jesus teaching people the truth about God
Describe how Jesus prayed for His disciples and for those who would believe in Him
Explain that the title Christ means the Anointed One and that Jesus was anointed by the Holy Spirit for His work
Identify Old Testament examples of prophets, priests, and kings being anointed for their offices
Explain how Jesus fulfills the promise of a Prophet like Moses and is greater than Moses
Restate in their own words the catechism definitions of how Christ executes the offices of prophet, priest, and king
Compare the three offices by matching each to the human need it meets, such as ignorance, guilt, and bondage to sin
Categorize Christ's priestly work into His once-for-all sacrifice and His continuing intercession
Describe the ways Christ exercises His kingly office in subduing, ruling, defending His people, and conquering His enemies
Analyze how Hebrews presents Christ as High Priest after the order of Melchizedek
Explain how Christ continues to exercise His prophetic office by His Word and Spirit, including through the Old Testament prophets and the apostles
Distinguish Christ's rule over all things from His special rule over His church
Analyze why the Old Testament kept the offices of priest and king separate and how Scripture foretells their union in the Messiah
Explain how the Heidelberg Catechism describes believers as sharing in Christ's anointing as prophets, priests, and kings
Contrast Christ's priesthood with the Levitical priesthood in its permanence, holiness, and sacrifice
Trace episodes in the Gospels where Jesus acts in each of His three offices
Explain how Hebrews presents Christ as God's final word and why the Reformed tradition holds that earlier ways of revelation have ceased
Construct a biblical account of Christ's ongoing intercession for His people at the Father's right hand
Evaluate views that reduce Christ to only a moral teacher or only a political king
Defend the sufficiency and finality of Christ's priesthood against views that add further sacrifices or human mediators
Explain how Calvin's treatment of the threefold office in the Institutes shaped later Reformed confessions
Write a synthesis showing how the three offices together present Christ as the only Mediator and Redeemer

changes: Kept and reworded the core competencies (identifying the offices, meaning of Christ, Prophet greater than Moses, comparing offices, sacrifice and intercession, Melchizedek, kingly rule, OT anointing, reductionist errors, finality of priesthood, only Mediator). Turned the Good Shepherd and prayer items into describable Gospel content. Dropped the humiliation and exaltation item as belonging to the sibling sub-topic. Added catechism definitions, the prophetic office by Word and Spirit, the kingdom of power versus the church, the separation and union of priest and king, believers sharing Christ's anointing, Levitical contrast, Gospel episodes, Christ as God's final word, and Calvin's influence. Replaced Keach's Q29 and WLC Q36 with more precise citations (WLC Q42-45, Q55, HC Q32, WCF 8.1, 1.1, 29.2).
